states.edition: 2021 Virginia Residential Code (VRC) — part of the 2021 Virginia Uniform Statewide Building Code (USBC/VCC, 13VAC5-63): 2021 IRC as amended by VCC Section 310.8
notes: The 2021 USBC took effect January 18, 2024 (DHCD memo of Nov 29, 2023); applicants could choose 2018 or 2021 technical provisions until January 17, 2025, and the 2021 edition has been mandatory for all new permit applications since January 18, 2025.

The 2024-based USBC is still in development (Board acted on 160+ proposals by Aug 2026); it is tentatively scheduled to take effect in October 2027 with a one-year transition, mandatory about October 2028, so the 2021 VRC is the edition in force on 2026-10-20.
VCC 310.8 item 20 changes R311.7.5.1 so the riser height shall be not more than 8-1/4 inches (210 mm), with the 3/8-inch variation limit and 4-inch-sphere open-riser rule kept.
VCC 310.8 item 21 changes R311.7.5.2 so the tread depth shall be not less than 9 inches (229 mm), with the 3/8-inch variation limit kept.
Guards (R312.1) and the deck section (R507) are not amended, so the IRC 36-inch guard and IRC prescriptive deck rules apply statewide.
VCC 103.4 item 3 lets each locality set its own Table R301.2(1) climatic and geographic design criteria, so frost depth, snow, wind and the rest come from the local building department.
Decks and open porches are added as Exception 6 to R302.1, so they are exempt from the exterior-wall fire-separation-distance requirements.

Decks are not in the statewide permit exemptions of VCC 108.2; only temporary ramps up to 30 inches and the building official's minor-and-ordinary-work exemption could apply, so localities set their own low-deck thresholds (Prince William uses 16-1/2 inches).
New R332.1 makes Appendix AH mandatory for patio covers, which matters for roofs over decks.
New R403.1 Exception 2 says footings are not required for ramps serving R-3/R-5 dwellings where the entrance is no more than 30 inches above grade.
R301.2.1 is amended so special wind regions and mountainous areas use 140 mph Vult at 4,000 ft elevation or higher and 110 mph below 4,000 ft.

A 2021 VCC snow-load error (ASCE 7-16 figures with ASCE 7-22 references) is being corrected by DHCD; until then Fairfax and Prince William say to use the VCC figures with ASCE 7-16 throughout, or ASCE 7-22 throughout, and never to mix the two.

states.edition: 2018 North Carolina State Building Code: Residential Code (2015 IRC with North Carolina amendments)
notes: The 2018 NC Residential Code (effective January 1, 2019) is still the code in force on 2026-10-20; the adopted 2024 NC Residential Code is not yet effective.

Under S.L. 2025-2 Sec. 5.12, the 2024 code takes effect 12 months after the first day of the month after the State Fire Marshal certifies that the code is published and the Residential Code Council is fully constituted. A June 1, 2026 state licensing-board notice says that has not happened and the earliest possible date is May 1, 2027.

The 2024 NC Residential Code is based on the 2021 IRC. It moves the deck rules out of Appendix M into a new Chapter 47 'Wood Decks' (in the 2024 code, Appendix AM is Home Day Care) and keeps the 8 1/4 in. riser, 9 in. tread and 36 in. guard.
Appendix M 'Wood Decks' is a North Carolina addition adopted as part of the code. It governs decks and roofed porches built under it, and computer deck-design programs may be accepted.

Deck post footings must be at least 12 in. below finished grade and sized by tributary area from Table AM102.1 (e.g. 8x16 in. for up to 36 sq ft, up to 24x24 in. for 150 sq ft). The statewide frost line depth is 12 in.

The deck band is attached to the house band per Table AM104.1: 5/8 in. hot-dip galvanized bolts plus 12d HDG nails, or self-drilling screws, spaced for 8 ft or 16 ft joist spans. On brick veneer, bolts only per Table AM104.1(2).
Aluminum flashing is not allowed; siding must not be left between the house band and the deck band, and the house needs a treated band or corrosion-resistant flashing (brick houses excepted).
Girder and joist span tables (AM105.2, AM106.1) are based on 40 psf live/snow load and 10 psf dead load, No. 2 wet-service lumber. Joists and girders may cantilever up to 1/4 of the adjacent span.
Maximum post height, from top of footing to bottom of girder, is 8 ft for 4x4 and 20 ft for 6x6 No. 2 SYP posts. Taller posts need a registered design professional.
No lateral bracing is needed for an attached deck under 4 ft high, or a freestanding deck 30 in. or less. Otherwise use knee braces, 2x6 cross bracing or post embedment (AM109).
Stair stringers may span at most 7 ft between supports and need at least 3 1/2 in. of wood behind the step cuts (AM110).
Decking must be No. 2 treated SYP or equivalent, with thickness by joist spacing from Table AM107.1 (e.g. 1 in. T&G at 16 in. o.c., 2 in. S4S at 24-36 in.).
NC deleted the IRC snow-load section (R301.2.3). Table R301.2(1) sets a statewide 20 psf roof load, 'Moderate' weathering, a 12 in. frost line, and termite protection required statewide.

notes: High-Velocity Hurricane Zone (HVHZ) = Miami-Dade and Broward counties: there FBC-R R301.1/R501.1 send structural work to FBC-R Chapter 44, which points to the FBC-Building HVHZ sections (1616-1626 loads, 2314-2330 wood), so the prescriptive R507 deck path does not govern; wind is fixed by FBC-B 1620.2 at 175 mph (Miami-Dade) / 170 mph (Broward) for Risk Category II, Exposure C unless D applies (1620.3), deck/balcony live loads follow ASCE 7 (1616.5), and joist hangers and devices need product approval (2319.3.3).

The 9th Edition (2026) FBC-R, on the 2024 IRC, takes effect Dec 31, 2026, so it is NOT in force on 2026-10-20; switch the row then (Miami-Dade applies it to applications filed on/after Dec 31, 2026, or online after 4 PM Dec 30, 2026).
Deck footings follow R403.1.4 (R507.3): at least 12 in. below finished grade; Florida has no frost line (the Table R301.2(1) frost-line footnote is Reserved).

Termite probability is 'very heavy' statewide (Table R301.2(1)); R318 requires a registered termiticide treatment with a Certificate of Compliance from the licensed pest-control company to the building department (R318.1).
If soil treatment is used, it must also go under all exterior concrete or grade within 1 ft of the house walls, with a vertical barrier after landscaping (R318.1.6).
All wood grade stakes, forms and other cellulose debris must be removed from under the building and within 1 ft of it, and wood may not be stored on the ground under any building (R318.6.3).

R318.7 requires 6 in. clearance between exterior wall coverings and final grade (4 in. above patio slabs); the R318.4 veneer exception needs a 6 in. clear inspection space above any adjoining deck, porch or soil.

In the FBC-R, deck ledger and lateral attachment are R507.8 and the Exterior guards section added in the 8th Edition is R507.9 (guard loads carried to the deck joists by a continuous load path), so cite Florida's section numbers, not the IRC's.
The 8th Edition removed ground-snow references from the deck tables (R507.5, R507.6, R507.8.1.3(1)), and Florida has no seismic provisions (R301.2.2 and FBC-B 1613 are Reserved).

Where Vult is 115 mph or more, R301.2.1.1 requires wind design by WFCM, ICC 600, ASCE 7, AISI S230, the FBC-Building or the MAF guide; the 8th Edition wind map (Figure R301.2(4)) follows ASCE 7-22, and the exposure category is set site by site (R301.2.1.4).
The coming 9th Edition adds R501.3: fasteners and connectors within 3,000 ft of a saltwater coastline must meet new R332.

counties.edition: 2021 Virginia Residential Code (2021 USBC); mandatory for applications since Jan 18, 2025

deck_notes: The county's Typical Deck Details (v2021.0, 1/5/2024, based on the 2021 VRC) cover single-level residential decks only, and any deviation needs county approval before construction.
Under the details, multi-level decks that share posts and footings are prohibited, as are privacy screens, planters, built-in seating, surface-mounted guard posts and hot tubs.
The details are designed for 40 psf live load plus 10 psf dead load, using preservative-treated #2 southern pine and G-185 or stainless hardware.
Footings must bear on solid ground 24 inches below grade, and county inspectors verify bearing before concrete is placed.
A footing whose edge is less than 5 ft from the house wall must bear at the same elevation as the house footings.
Footing types A to H run from 12 in. square / 14 in. round by 6 in. thick up to 26 in. square / 29 in. round by 10 in. thick, using 3,000 psi concrete.
Posts must be 6x6 (4x4 allowed up to 2.5 ft tall), with a maximum height of up to 14 ft set by Table 4.
The ledger must be at least 2x8 and no shallower than the joists, with continuous flashing at wood-framed walls and no lead anchors.
Attaching the ledger through brick or stone veneer, to open-web floor trusses, to chimneys or to overhangs is prohibited, so those cases need a free-standing deck or an engineered design.
A guard is required where the deck is more than 30 in. above grade at a point 36 in. from its edge; it must be at least 36 in. high and stop a 4-in. sphere.
Guard posts must not be notched and must be fastened with hold-down anchors rated at least 1,800 lb.
Stairs need risers of 8-1/4 in. max, treads of 9 in. min and a width of at least 36 in., with an intermediate free-standing landing where the total rise is more than 12 ft.
Hidden decking fasteners combined with posts over 2.5 ft tall require continuous 2x6 diagonal bracing under the joists.
A copy of the details with Section 10 (deck design record and sketch) filled in, plus the approved plat and building plans, must be on the job site for inspections.
Required inspections are footing (holes dug and ledger attached), framing and final; framing can be skipped if the joists are more than 48 in. above grade.

Technical Bulletin 24-1 (2/9/2024) lets LDS accept a house location plat instead of a grading-plan revision for an uncovered standalone deck on a lot with active bonded grading plans, if no impervious features or grade, utility, easement or tree-area changes are involved.
counties.note: Design criteria come from the LDS Codes and Standards page ('Local Design Load Criteria'). That page also lists a winter design temperature of 17°F, required ice-shield underlayment, NFIP entry 3/5/1990, air freezing index <=1500, mean annual temperature 50°F and decay 'slight to moderate'. It still says the county 'references the 2018 International Codes' but also states that all applications since Jan 18, 2025 must meet the 2021 USBC. Snow caveat: 25 psf is valid only when designing with the VCC Figures 1608.2 and ASCE 7-16 throughout; with ASCE 7-22 the snow load comes from ASCE 7-22 maps, pending a DHCD correction. Deck permit threshold, number of plan copies and paper size are not stated in the documents I opened.

deck_notes: A building permit is required before building a deck. Decks get an open-footing inspection, a framing inspection and a final inspection.
Footings must be dug into undisturbed soil at least 12 in. below finished grade, sized by tributary area per Table AM102.1 (e.g. 8x16 in. minimum for 30 sq ft).
Guards at least 36 in. high are required where the walking surface is more than 30 in. above finished grade; a 4 in. sphere must not pass.
Guard rail posts may be at most 8 ft o.c., attached to the outer bands with two 3/8 in. galvanized bolts. A 4x4 post may not be notched, per an NC DOI interpretation.
Stairs: 8 1/4 in. maximum riser and 9 in. minimum tread (plus 3/4 in. nosing), at least 36 in. wide.
Stairs need a handrail on one side with 4 or more risers; at 30 in. or more of rise, open sides need a combined guard/handrail 34-38 in. high.

Lateral bracing is required when the deck is 48 in. or more from top of footing to deck floor, and for self-supported decks of any height (AM109). Posts must be anchored at the top with approved straps or post brackets.
Attached decks connect to the house band with 5/8 in. galvanized through-bolts per Table AM104.1. Siding other than brick must be removed so the deck band fully contacts the house band.
Non-aluminum, corrosion-resistant flashing is required between the house band and the deck band.
Joists are sized for a 40 psf live load. Cantilevered joists and girders must be No. 1 grade SYP; a cantilevered girder carries floor loads only, no roof loads.
Decks are excluded from the 100 sq ft enclosed-addition trigger for Mecklenburg's residential plan review. Converting a deck to a sunroom needs a full masonry foundation with a continuous footing.

Elevated walking surfaces with an impervious moisture barrier need full barrier details and the manufacturer's instructions (107.2.5).
The parcel's wind speed comes from the county's GIS wind-speed tool at discover.pbcgov.org/pzb/Maps/WindSpeeds.aspx.
Footings at least 12 in. below finished grade (FBC-R R403.1.4); there is no frost line.
counties.note: HVHZ: no. Wind varies by zone on the county map: 170 mph from the coast west to the 160-mph line (the whole urban east, including West Palm Beach, Boca Raton, Delray, Boynton, Jupiter and Wellington), 160 mph in the central band, and 150 mph in the western Glades (Belle Glade, Pahokee); 170 is given because most homes are in the 170 zone. frost_depth_in 0 because there is no frost line (FBC-R Table R301.2(1) frost footnote Reserved); deck footings go at least 12 in. below finished grade (R507.3 -> R403.1.4). Ground snow NA -> 0. seismic_sdc null because the FBC has no seismic provisions (FBC-B 1613 / FBC-R R301.2.2 Reserved), which in practice means the same as SDC A. Weathering and termite are from the statewide FBC-R Table R301.2(1). The county's online submittal checklists date from 2005 (FBC 2004), so the current 8th Edition amendments were used for the deck notes.
